limitations: Artifact identity is unavailable for this observation.
REA attaches to an already-running exact target. It does not launch the target, evaluate JavaScript, install breakpoints, or send pause/resume commands.
Enabling Debugger can make target-authored debugger statements pause execution; observation does not suppress or resume these pauses.
Only Runtime.enable and Debugger.enable are sent; source text, object values, EventEmitter activity, and Electron IPC are not inspected.
The selected endpoint and target ID authorize observation; discovery file locations can remain unresolved and do not prove filesystem identity.
Node discovery reports a best-effort pathname rather than an encoded file URL; lossy Windows paths and ambiguous underscores are preserved without guessing a file path.
Every target exposed by the selected Inspector endpoint is eligible for observation; target IDs and locations are not authenticated as operating-system process identity.
No runtime graph depth is traversed because passive Inspector events do not establish require/import caller edges.
Runtime host platform and architecture were not observed.

provider.name: REA Chrome DevTools Protocol observation provider

limitations: Artifact identity is unavailable for this observation.
Observation starts when REA attaches; prior network and console activity is unavailable.

Worker targets are a final inventory snapshot, not worker-session observation. Their attached flag describes any debugging client; this page-session collector does not observe worker network, console, or script events, and short-lived workers may be absent from the snapshot.

Raw network headers, bodies, cookies, storage values, console objects, and WebSocket payloads are never retained; explicitly requested primitive console text is retained verbatim, while payload captures retain value-free shapes.
Source maps are reported only as declarative URLs and are not fetched.
URL-less scripts and console events without an allowed source URL are excluded because their origin cannot be proven.
CDP discovery could not establish the target's debugger attachment state.
Browser host platform and architecture were not observed.
